The shipped artifacts confirm this: the release workflow builds `cargo build --locked --release -p quarry` with default features (.github/workflows/release-build.yml:62), and the Dockerfile builds with default features unless the operator explicitly sets the QUARRY_FEATURES build-arg. The project's own threat model states the shipped image is tmp-documents-only, that the `/v1/libraries/**` surface 'has no access control at all' and 'must not be internet-exposed', and explicitly lists 'git sync — quarry-git' as out of scope because 'its handlers take request-controlled local paths and remote URLs (arbitrary FS + SSRF). Reachable only in a `lib-documents` build' (docs/security/threat-model.md:162-166, 324). Reaching the sink therefore requires (a) a non-default, explicitly opt-in build that the threat model declares out of scope and unsafe to expose, and (b) non-loopback binding, since the server defaults to 127.0.0.1:7831 (crates/quarry-cli/src/lib.rs:261) and loudly warns on non-loopback binds (crates/quarry-server/src/lib.rs:692-705). Sink: the ExpiresAt arm stores the string unchanged (crates/quarry-storage/src/tmp_documents.rs:198) and writes it raw via UPDATE ... SET expires_at = ?1 (tmp_documents.rs:238-243); the PATCH ttl path set_tmp_document_ttl rejects only null and UPDATEs the raw string (tmp_documents.rs:388-416, 406-411), and TtlRequest is an unvalidated Option<String> (crates/quarry-server/src/lib.rs:962-965). Enforcement is purely lexicographic: tmp reads require `expires_at > ?2` with ?2 = current RFC3339 timestamp (crates/quarry-storage/src/lib.rs:1502-1508) and expiry detection uses `expires_at <= ?2` (lib.rs:1405-1411), against a 30-day default (lib.rs:1368-1370). No defense exists anywhere between: (1) a repo-wide search for parse_from_rfc3339/DateTime parsing shows parsing only on unrelated paths (session.rs:1049, versions.rs:371 history provenance, quarry-fuse); (2) the read-back type Timestamp is a bare string newtype (crates/quarry-core/src/lib.rs:97; row.rs:36 reads it with opt_text, no parse), so no deserialization validation occurs; (3) no sweeper/reaper exists in code at all — grep for sweeper/tombstone/expired-cleanup in crates/ finds only the two string comparisons, and the threat model itself lists 'Clamp expires_at server-side on create and update (T13)' as an open action item noting the value is currently 'unclamped' (docs/security/threat-model.md:82-84, 502-508). Consequently a far-future value like '9999-12-31T00:00:00.000Z' — or even 'z', which sorts after any '20..' timestamp — keeps an anonymously created document permanently live, defeating the 30-day lifecycle, exactly as claimed. LOW severity as reported is appropriate; the claim as written is accurate."}
